text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Social Democrat leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa says 1997 budget is "conservative and does not reform anything". In an interview with the paper, he adds: "The budget does not create employment and does raise taxes".
- Credito Predial Portugues posted 3.3 billion escudos net profit in the first nine months of 1996, 5.3 percent more than in the same period in 1995.

- Grundig Industria Portugal (GIP) planning to lay off 700 workers which would cost the company two billion escudos in compensation, according to the workers' commission. Grundig is trying to transfer surplus workers to Bosch.

- Right-wing Popular Party said yesterday it could let the 1997 budget pass in parliament in a vote set for December 11. Communist Party will vote against the budget and Social Democratic Party will abstain.
- Electricity company EDP to be privatised in the second quarter of 1997 is negotiating to buy a minority position in private mobile phone company Telecel. Telecel due to be floated on December 9.
- Some 100 companies are negotiating the payment of their tax and social security debts. The state could rake in 20 billion escudos of revenues.
- Parliament will start discussing the 1997 budget today with the focus on progress to join Economic and Monetary Union and on the level of taxation.
- Petrol prices will rise at midnight, Under-Secretary for Industry and Energy Jose Penedos said.
